– Today, Ubisoft released its earnings figures for the first half of fiscal 2026-27.
Yves Guillemot, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, said

“In the first half of FY2026-27, we continued to make tangible progress on our strategic and operational priorities. Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio.

Our new operating model is now fully in place, with leadership secured across all Creative Houses. In an increasingly competitive entertainment industry, gamers require exceptional quality, distinctive creative experiences, uncompromising gameplay and a defined audience for games to stand out and succeed. By repositioning our talents at the center of decision-making and fostering a more spontaneous and direct link with our communities, our new model is designed precisely to deliver on these imperatives. Its first benefits are already visible, with the commercial success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and the renewed momentum of Rainbow Six Siege.

We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences.

We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle. In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.
We are confirming our FY2026-27 objectives. By combining our iconic brands and creative talent with a more focused, agile and accountable operating model, we are building a stronger Ubisoft.”

Net bookings stood at €389m this quarter, above guidance of around €370m. The outperformance was mainly driven by Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced, while the rest of the catalog, including the Assassin’s Creed catalog, the Ghost Recon franchise and Invincible: Guarding the Globe, saw strong performances. Excluding partnerships, net bookings were up over 50% year-on-year. Back-catalog bookings stood at €218m, down 55%, reflecting a high comparison base that included partnerships and the significant contribution of Assassin’s Creed Shadows. Excluding partnerships, back-catalog was down a high single-digit percentage year-on-year.

Overall, net bookings for the semester stood at €645m, down 17% year-on-year, or up double-digits excluding partnerships. MAUs and Unique Active Players across Consoles and PC respectively stood at 34 and 88 million, stable versus last year.

Ubisoft also announced the launch of The Player Council on PC, a platform that allows players to test prototypes and games in development and share their feedback directly with the teams. It reflects the Group’s commitment to placing players at the heart of development from the earliest stages, and to strengthening its engagement with the PC community, the industry’s most dynamic platform.
New Operating Model now fully in place

Ubisoft has just completed the rollout of its new operating model, marking an important milestone in the Group’s transformation. This model represents a radical change. It is built around Creative Houses, fully accountable for their P&L, whose purpose is to reposition creative talents at the center of decision-making and foster more direct and spontaneous relations with gamer communities.

Creative House 2, which includes iconic franchises like The Division, Ghost Recon and Splinter Cell® alongside March of Giants, has been named Massive Entertainment. Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms. With the appointment of an external General Manager for Creative House 4, who will join in January, all Creative House leadership positions are now filled.
The new organization is complemented by two dedicated units:

Motherbrain, the team behind Teammates, the Group’s first playable generative AI experience, has been established as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technology for new forms of gameplay. Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds. It aims to serve creators globally, both within Ubisoft’s Creative House ecosystem and beyond, and form partnerships with selected technology actors.

In addition, a dedicated unit has been created to maximize the value of the Group’s brands outside the Creative Houses’ portfolios as well as explore new opportunities leveraging innovative gameplay supported by new technologies, through an agile and investment-light model.

This new organization responds to a profound shift in the industry. Games that stand out today combine a strong creative identity with uncompromising gameplay, exceptional quality, and are first built for a passionate, well-defined audience. The Creative Houses are designed precisely to deliver on these imperatives, empowering creative talents and fostering more intimate connections with players.
The first benefits of this new organization are already visible with Vantage Studios celebrating its first year of existence on October 1.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced illustrates its ability to deliver games that players love and that also perform financially. The newly formed Assassin’s Creed leadership made clear, decisive choices in the final stretch of development. This enabled the game to achieve an elevated level of quality and a commercial performance that positions Black Flag Resynced among the industry’s most successful Action-Adventure remakes.

Rainbow Six Siege demonstrates the impact of clear accountability on Live operations as well as the benefits of a closer engagement with its community of fans. Taking into account their feedback, the team has swiftly refocused the game on its tactical and competitive core, with sustained investment in core gameplay, anti-cheat and a faster content cadence. This has driven a strong recovery in player activity since late 2025. The game has ranked among the top 10 across Xbox and PlayStation combined in terms of MAU over H1 FY2026-27.

The Group’s third phase of its cost reduction program, targeting a fixed cost base3 of €1.25bn on a run-rate basis by March 2028 remains firmly on track. The H1 FY2026-27 fixed cost base stood at €660m, down 6% year-on-year. Headcount was down close to 1,100 over the semester.

IFRS 15 sales for the second quarter of 2026-27 came to €405.5 million, up 16.8% (or 16.6% at constant exchange rates4) on the €347.1 million generated in second-quarter 2025-26. For the first half of 2026-27, IFRS 15 sales totaled €673.6 million, up 2.4% (or 2.5% at constant exchange rates4) compared with the first half 2025-26 figure of €657.8 million.

Net bookings for the second quarter of 2026-27 totaled €388.9 million, down 20.8% (or 20.9% at constant exchange rates4) compared with the €490.8 million recorded for the second-quarter of 2025-26. First half 2026-27 net bookings amounted to €644.7 million, down 16.5% (or 16.5% at constant exchange rates4) on the €772.4 million generated in the first-half 2025-26.
Non-IFRS operating income came in at €(155.9) million, versus €27.1 million in the first half 2025-26.

Non-IFRS attributable net income amounted to €(199.4) million, representing non-IFRS diluted earnings per share of €(1.48), compared with non-IFRS attributable net income of €(37.0) million and non-IFRS diluted earnings per share of €(0.28) in first half 2025-26.

IFRS attributable net income for H1 2026-27 totaled €(254.5) million, representing IFRS diluted EPS of €(1.89), compared with IFRS attributable net income of €(161.3) million and IFRS diluted earnings per share of €(1.23) in first-half 2025-26.

Non-IFRS cash flows from operating activities represented a net cash outflow of €(323.9) million in H1 2026-27 (versus a net cash outflow of €(240.3) million in first half 2025-26). It reflects a negative €(249.0) million in non-IFRS cash flow from operations (versus a negative €(138.9) million in H1 2025-26) and a €(74.9) million increase in non-IFRS working capital requirement (compared with a €(101.5) million increase in the first six months 2025-26).
Main balance sheet items and liquidity

At September 30, 2026, Equity attributable to owners of the parent company was €1,244 million, down year-on-year, and its non-IFRS net debt was €541 million versus non-IFRS net debt of €1,149 million at September 30, 2025. IFRS net debt totaled €775 million at September 30, 2026, of which €233 million related to the IFRS16 accounting restatement. At September 30, 2026, Cash and cash equivalents stood at €1,029.8 million.
Net bookings for the third quarter of 2026-27 are expected to come in at around €250m, reflecting, as expected, the particularly crowded holiday season.
The Company confirms its targets for 2026-27 and expects:
Net bookings down by a high single-digit percentage,
A high single-digit negative non-IFRS operating margin,
Free Cash Flow consumption of no more than €500m.

The second half of the fiscal year will notably benefit from the releases of Rayman® Legends Retold and Just Dance®: Decades of Hits, continued Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced sales, other targeted premium titles based on established Ubisoft brands to be announced in the coming months, continued Live Services content updates including a strong Q4 for Siege with the launch of Year 12 and material contribution from partnerships. Free Cash Flow in the second half will also be supported by the continued reduction of the fixed cost base and better working capital variation than in the first half.

The Group expects a significantly stronger and diversified pipeline of content to come over FY2027-28 and FY2028-29, supported by releases across its major brands including Assassin’s Creed, Far Cry® and Ghost Recon as well as an acceleration of its Live Services driven by Rainbow Six Siege. In this context, the Group expects to get back to Free Cash Flow generation and positive non-IFRS EBIT in FY2027-28 and generate robust Free Cash Flow in FY2028-29, with positive cumulated Free Cash Flow during the FY2026-27 to FY2028-29 period.

Ubisoft is a creator of worlds, committed to enriching players’ lives with original and memorable entertainment experiences. Ubisoft’s global teams create and develop a deep and diverse portfolio of games, featuring brands such as Assassin’s Creed®, Brawlhalla®, For Honor®, Far Cry®, Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon®, Just Dance®, Rabbids®, Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six®, The Crew® and Tom Clancy’s The Division®. Through Ubisoft Connect, players can enjoy an ecosystem of services to enhance their gaming experience, get rewards and connect with friends across platforms. With Ubisoft+, the subscription service, they can access a growing catalog of more than 100 Ubisoft games and DLC. For the 2025-26 fiscal year, Ubisoft generated net bookings of €1.53 billion. Alternative Performance Indicators, not presented in the financial statements, are:
Net bookings corresponds to IFRS 15 sales adjusted for the following items (positive or negative):
the unconditional commitments related to license or distribution agreements,
financing impacts (financing components and price reductions);
Player Recurring Investment (PRI) corresponds to sales of digital items, DLC, season passes, subscriptions and advertising;
Non-IFRS operating profit corresponds to operating profit less the following items (positive or negative):
the difference between net bookings and IFRS 15 sales,
stock-based compensation paid under free share award plans and Group savings plans,
depreciation of acquired intangible assets with indefinite useful lives,
non-operating income and expenses resulting from restructuring operations within the Group;
Non-IFRS operating margin corresponds to Non-IFRS operating income expressed as a percentage of net bookings. This ratio is an indicator of the Group’s financial performance;
Non-IFRS net income corresponds to net income less the following items:
the above-described deductions used to calculate Non-IFRS operating income,
income and expenses arising on revaluations, carried out after the measurement period, of the potential variable consideration granted in relation to business combinations,
OCEANE bonds’ interest expense recognized in accordance with IFRS 9,
the tax impacts on these adjustments;
Non-IFRS attributable net income corresponds to Non-IFRS net income attributable to owners of the parent;
Non-IFRS diluted EPS corresponds to Non-IFRS attributable net income divided by the weighted average number of shares after exercise of the rights attached to dilutive instruments.
The adjusted cash flow statement includes:
Non-IFRS cash flow from operations which comprises:

the costs of internally developed software and external developments (presented under cash flows from investing activities in the IFRS cash flow statement) as these costs are an integral part of the Group’s operations,
the restatement of impacts (after tax) related to the difference between net bookings and IFRS 15 sales,
the restatement of commitments related to leases due to the application of IFRS 16,

Non-IFRS change in working capital requirement which includes movements in deferred taxes and restates the impacts (after tax) related to the difference between net bookings and IFRS 15 sales, thus canceling out the income or expenses presented in Non-IFRS cash flow from operations;
Non-IFRS cash flows from operating activities which includes:
the costs of internal and external licenses development (presented under cash flows from investing activities in the IFRS cash flow statement),
the restatement of lease commitments relating to the application of IFRS 16 presented under IFRS in cash flow from financing activities;
Non-IFRS cash flows from investing activities which excludes the costs of internal and external licenses development that are presented under Non-IFRS cash flow from operations;

Free cash flow corresponds to cash flows from Non-IFRS operating activities after cash inflows/outflows arising on the disposal/acquisition of other intangible assets and property, plant and equipment and lease commitments related to the application of IFRS 16;
Cash flow from Non-IFRS financing activities, which excludes lease commitments related to the application of IFRS 16 presented in Non-IFRS cash flow;
IFRS net cash/(debt) position corresponds to cash and cash equivalents and financial assets used for cash management, less financial liabilities excluding derivatives;
Non-IFRS net cash/(debt) position corresponds to the net cash/(debt) position as adjusted for commitments related to leases (IFRS 16).
